# switch

## Expression Switch

Switch di Go lebih bersih dan aman daripada di C/Java. **Tidak ada fallthrough otomatis** — setiap case berhenti setelah dieksekusi (tanpa perlu `break`):

```go
hari := "Senin"

switch hari {
case "Sabtu", "Minggu":
    fmt.Println("Akhir pekan!")
case "Senin":
    fmt.Println("Awal pekan, semangat!")
case "Jumat":
    fmt.Println("Hampir akhir pekan!")
default:
    fmt.Println("Hari biasa")
}
// Output: Awal pekan, semangat!
```

## Multiple Values dalam Satu Case

```go
bulan := 4

switch bulan {
case 3, 4, 5:
    fmt.Println("Musim Semi")
case 6, 7, 8:
    fmt.Println("Musim Panas")
case 9, 10, 11:
    fmt.Println("Musim Gugur")
case 12, 1, 2:
    fmt.Println("Musim Dingin")
}
// Output: Musim Semi
```

## Switch Tanpa Ekspresi (Seperti if-else)

```go
suhu := 38.5

switch {
case suhu >= 40:
    fmt.Println("Demam tinggi!")
case suhu >= 38:
    fmt.Println("Demam")
case suhu >= 37:
    fmt.Println("Sedikit panas")
default:
    fmt.Println("Normal")
}
// Output: Demam
```

## Keyword `fallthrough`

Gunakan `fallthrough` untuk meneruskan eksekusi ke case berikutnya (eksplisit):

```go
x := 1

switch x {
case 1:
    fmt.Println("satu")
    fallthrough  // terus ke case 2
case 2:
    fmt.Println("dua")
    fallthrough  // terus ke case 3
case 3:
    fmt.Println("tiga")
case 4:
    fmt.Println("empat")  // tidak dieksekusi
}
// Output:
// satu
// dua
// tiga
```

**Perhatian:** `fallthrough` tidak memeriksa kondisi case berikutnya!

## Type Switch

Type switch digunakan untuk memeriksa tipe dinamis dari interface:

```go
func describe(i interface{}) string {
    switch v := i.(type) {
    case int:
        return fmt.Sprintf("int: %d", v)
    case string:
        return fmt.Sprintf("string: %q", v)
    case bool:
        return fmt.Sprintf("bool: %t", v)
    case []int:
        return fmt.Sprintf("[]int len=%d", len(v))
    default:
        return fmt.Sprintf("unknown type: %T", v)
    }
}

fmt.Println(describe(42))             // int: 42
fmt.Println(describe("hello"))        // string: "hello"
fmt.Println(describe(true))           // bool: true
fmt.Println(describe([]int{1, 2, 3})) // []int len=3
fmt.Println(describe(3.14))           // unknown type: float64
```

## Switch vs if-else Chain

| Aspek | switch | if-else chain |
|---|---|---|
| Keterbacaan | Lebih bersih untuk banyak kasus | Verbosity lebih |
| Fallthrough | Eksplisit dengan `fallthrough` | Tidak ada |
| Type checking | Type switch | Type assertion berulang |
| Performa | Bisa lebih cepat (jump table) | Linear check |
content_en:
# switch

## Expression Switch

Switch in Go is cleaner and safer than in C/Java. **There is no automatic fallthrough** — each case stops after execution (no `break` needed):

```go
day := "Monday"

switch day {
case "Saturday", "Sunday":
    fmt.Println("Weekend!")
case "Monday":
    fmt.Println("Start of the week, stay motivated!")
case "Friday":
    fmt.Println("Almost the weekend!")
default:
    fmt.Println("Regular day")
}
// Output: Start of the week, stay motivated!
```

## Multiple Values in One Case

```go
month := 4

switch month {
case 3, 4, 5:
    fmt.Println("Spring")
case 6, 7, 8:
    fmt.Println("Summer")
case 9, 10, 11:
    fmt.Println("Autumn")
case 12, 1, 2:
    fmt.Println("Winter")
}
// Output: Spring
```

## Switch Without Expression (Like if-else)

```go
temp := 38.5

switch {
case temp >= 40:
    fmt.Println("High fever!")
case temp >= 38:
    fmt.Println("Fever")
case temp >= 37:
    fmt.Println("Slightly warm")
default:
    fmt.Println("Normal")
}
// Output: Fever
```

## The `fallthrough` Keyword

Use `fallthrough` to explicitly continue execution to the next case:

```go
x := 1

switch x {
case 1:
    fmt.Println("one")
    fallthrough  // continue to case 2
case 2:
    fmt.Println("two")
    fallthrough  // continue to case 3
case 3:
    fmt.Println("three")
case 4:
    fmt.Println("four")  // not executed
}
// Output:
// one
// two
// three
```

**Warning:** `fallthrough` does NOT check the next case's condition!

## Type Switch

A type switch is used to check the dynamic type of an interface value:

```go
func describe(i interface{}) string {
    switch v := i.(type) {
    case int:
        return fmt.Sprintf("int: %d", v)
    case string:
        return fmt.Sprintf("string: %q", v)
    case bool:
        return fmt.Sprintf("bool: %t", v)
    case []int:
        return fmt.Sprintf("[]int len=%d", len(v))
    default:
        return fmt.Sprintf("unknown type: %T", v)
    }
}

fmt.Println(describe(42))             // int: 42
fmt.Println(describe("hello"))        // string: "hello"
fmt.Println(describe(true))           // bool: true
fmt.Println(describe([]int{1, 2, 3})) // []int len=3
fmt.Println(describe(3.14))           // unknown type: float64
```

## switch vs if-else Chain

| Aspect | switch | if-else chain |
|---|---|---|
| Readability | Cleaner for many cases | More verbose |
| Fallthrough | Explicit with `fallthrough` | None |
| Type checking | Type switch | Repeated type assertions |
| Performance | Can be faster (jump table) | Linear check |

quiz.question_id: Mengapa `switch` Go biasanya tidak memerlukan `break` di akhir setiap `case`?
quiz.question_en: Why does a Go `switch` usually not need `break` at the end of each `case`?
options_id: Karena setiap `case` berhenti sendiri kecuali diberi `fallthrough` secara eksplisit
Karena `switch` Go hanya boleh punya satu `case`
Karena compiler selalu mengubah `switch` menjadi `if` tunggal
options_en: Because `break` is automatically added only for `default`
Because each `case` stops on its own unless `fallthrough` is explicitly used
Because a Go `switch` may only have one `case`
Because the compiler always rewrites a `switch` into a single `if`

Itu berfungsi seperti rantai `if / else if` berbasis kondisi boolean
Itu hanya valid untuk type switch
options_en: It is only shorthand for `for {}`
It is used only for pointer comparisons
It behaves like an `if / else if` chain based on boolean conditions
It is only valid for type switches

quiz.question_id: Apa efek tepat dari `fallthrough` dalam switch Go?
quiz.question_en: What is the exact effect of `fallthrough` in a Go switch?
options_id: Memaksa eksekusi lanjut ke `case` berikutnya tanpa mengecek kondisinya
options_en: It runs `default` after the current `case`
It re-checks the conditions of all following `case`s
It forces execution to continue to the next `case` without checking its condition
It repeats the current `case` one more time

quiz.question_en: What is the full output of the `x := 1` example that uses two `fallthrough`s?
options_en: `one` and then stop
`one`, `two`, `three`
`one`, `three`
`two`, `three`

quiz.question_id: Dalam `switch v := i.(type)`, apa yang benar tentang `v` di dalam setiap `case`?
quiz.question_en: In `switch v := i.(type)`, what is true about `v` inside each `case`?
options_id: `v` memiliki tipe konkret yang cocok dengan `case` yang sedang dijalankan
`v` selalu berupa pointer ke nilai asli
options_en: `v` always remains of type `interface{}`
`v` has the concrete type that matches the currently executing `case`
`v` is always a pointer to the original value
`v` can only be used in `default`

quiz.question_id: Kapan type switch lebih tepat dipakai daripada expression switch biasa?
quiz.question_en: When is a type switch more appropriate than a regular expression switch?
options_id: Saat ingin memeriksa tipe dinamis dari nilai interface
Saat ingin membandingkan banyak integer sekaligus
options_en: When you want to inspect the dynamic type of an interface value
When you want to compare many integers at once
When you want to avoid `default`
When you need alphabetically ordered `case`s

quiz.question_id: Jika beberapa nilai harus memicu cabang yang sama, fitur mana yang paling tepat: `case 3, 4, 5:` atau `fallthrough`?
quiz.question_en: If several values should trigger the same branch, which is more appropriate: `case 3, 4, 5:` or `fallthrough`?
options_id: Gunakan `fallthrough`, karena itu memeriksa semua nilai satu per satu
Gunakan banyak nilai dalam satu `case`, karena itu langsung menyatakan himpunan nilai yang sama
Gunakan keduanya selalu bersama agar aman
options_en: Use `fallthrough`, because it checks all values one by one
Use multiple values in one `case`, because it directly states the set of equivalent values
Always use both together to be safe
There is no difference at all

quiz.question_id: Jika `temp := 41.0` dimasukkan ke switch tanpa ekspresi dengan urutan `>= 40`, `>= 38`, `>= 37`, output mana yang benar?
quiz.question_en: If `temp := 41.0` is used with an expressionless switch ordered as `>= 40`, `>= 38`, `>= 37`, which output is correct?
options_id: `Demam` karena semua case true akan dijalankan
`Demam tinggi!` karena case true pertama yang cocok dijalankan
options_en: `Fever` because all true cases will run
`Slightly warm` because the last case wins
`High fever!` because the first matching true case runs
No output without `fallthrough`
